App Privacy nutrition labels vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume filing privacy nutrition labels covers storefront language. Connect actually separates compliance disclosures from marketing copy:

  • App Privacy questionnaire & nutrition labels — structured data-type disclosures Apple renders in the Privacy Details section. You file these in App Store Connect under App Privacy. They do not generate Chinese listing text.
  • Privacy policy URL — legal document linked from Connect. AppLocale does not draft or localize privacy-policy legal text.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of nutrition-label accuracy.

Accurate nutrition labels and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe privacy on the product page in zh-Hans, not how you file the questionnaire.

What China buyers see when zh-Hans privacy copy is missing

Privacy-forward apps often lead marketing screenshots with Privacy Details panels, data-collection summaries, or trust badges — surfaces where English system chrome and your marketing blurbs appear together:

  • English title and subtitle — app name and tagline still Latin script while competitors show native Chinese privacy positioning
  • Untranslated privacy badges — overlay lines like "Privacy First", "No Tracking", "Data Not Collected", or "We don't track" remain English on zh-Hans gallery frames
  • Privacy value in English — description opens with US privacy marketing ("Your data never leaves your device") that China readers skim past or misread
  • Keyword field still en-US — buyers search 隐私, 不跟踪, 数据安全, or 本地存储; an English-only keyword row misses China Search intent
  • Mixed page — Chinese description pasted once but screenshot captions and subtitle still English — reads unfinished next to localized competitors
  • Over-claiming in machine translation — stiff 翻译腔 that guarantees "100% private" or "zero data ever" when your nutrition labels list contact info or usage analytics

Better zh-Hans listing copy helps privacy-conscious buyers understand your data practices before install. It does not replace accurate App Privacy disclosures, privacy-policy legal text, or Apple's review decisions.

Privacy-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Privacy-forward listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers evaluate trust claims — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Product page vs Privacy Details panel

Your listing can summarize privacy in buyer-friendly language — 不跟踪用户, 数据仅存于设备, 最小化收集 — but must stay consistent with what Apple's Privacy Details section already shows from your nutrition labels. AppLocale aligns storefront phrasing with your English claims and stated data practices; we do not contradict filed disclosures.

Avoiding "100% private" over-claims

US pages sometimes use "100% private", "zero data collection", or "completely anonymous" when nutrition labels still list identifiers, diagnostics, or purchase history. Chinese copy should use factual, defensible phrasing — not superlatives that invite review scrutiny or mislead buyers who compare listing text to Privacy Details.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need privacy-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 隐私, 不跟踪, and 数据安全 each signal different intent from generic productivity keywords.

Screenshot captions on privacy frames

Gallery frames that show Privacy Details panels, data-collection summaries, or trust badges need one-line zh-Hans captions — "不跟踪用户，数据仅存于设备" not "Privacy First" burned into the product page story.

Common mistakes on privacy-themed zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming nutrition labels localize automatically — App Privacy filed in Connect; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and Privacy First screenshot caption lines still English
  • Contradicting filed nutrition labels — listing says "no data collected" when Connect shows contact info or analytics types
  • Promising "100% private" in zh-Hans — absolute claims that do not match Privacy Details or invite App Review questions
  • Conflating listing copy with privacy-policy legal text — description paragraphs are marketing copy, not substitutes for your privacy URL document
  • English Privacy First on zh-Hans screenshots — Connect caption fields are Chinese but burned-in trust badges on PNG exports are still Latin
  • Expecting AppLocale to file nutrition labels — questionnaire completion and label submission are outside listing rewrite scope
  • What's New still English after privacy launch — see What's New in Simplified Chinese when privacy features shipped in a recent version

FAQ

Does filing App Privacy nutrition labels auto-translate my China listing?

No. Nutrition labels and the App Privacy questionnaire control what Apple shows in Privacy Details — they do not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback.

What can zh-Hans listing copy say about privacy vs what the nutrition label already shows?

Listing copy should summarize privacy in plain language aligned with your filed disclosures — without contradicting Connect or implying guarantees Apple does not support. AppLocale rewrites from your English claims and stated data practices; we do not invent privacy behavior.

Does AppLocale file or submit nutrition labels?

No. We deliver Connect listing metadata copy only — name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot caption lines. Questionnaire filing, label submission, and privacy-policy legal drafting are outside scope.

How should zh-Hans listing copy avoid over-claiming privacy?

Avoid absolute claims like 100% private or zero data unless they match your nutrition labels and actual product behavior. Use factual phrasing — 不跟踪用户, 数据仅存于设备, 最小化收集 — that mirrors what buyers read in Privacy Details.

What character limits apply to zh-Hans privacy listing fields?

App name and subtitle are each up to 30 characters on the zh-Hans row. The keyword field allows up to 100 characters. Description and screenshot caption lines have longer limits but privacy claims should stay concise — especially subtitle and overlay lines on privacy-themed frames.

What do I send after AppLocale payment?

Your live App Store listing URL, current English listing copy, screenshot overlay lines that mention privacy (with frame order noted), a brief summary of what your nutrition labels disclose, and target locale (zh-Hans). Reply from the email address on your Stripe receipt — we deliver to that Stripe email within 24 hours.

Will zh-Hans privacy copy improve China rankings?

We do not guarantee ranking, browse placement, or download lift. Complete zh-Hans metadata helps users who already find your page understand privacy claims in their language — it is not a placement hack.
